How these sit against the SA hamper market

Published SA gift hampers run from R199.95 (Richmeats gift box) and R295 (Richmeats standard hamper) up to R720 (buildyourbasket.co.za deluxe). Our Silver box is built and delivered as a corporate gifting piece rather than a supermarket hamper, so it is priced above that band — and we would rather tell you that than have you discover it in a procurement comparison.

The previous Silver entry price was R3,000. It is now R2,650 — a 12% reduction, applied because the box no longer carries an item whose import paperwork was incomplete.

Biltong price ladder

We corrected our own ladder.

Two of our prices were wrong in a way that worked against us: the 500g pack cost more per kilo than the 1kg, and the 7kg case cost more than buying seven 1kg boxes. A buyer doing the arithmetic on our own sheet would have been right to take it. Both are fixed.

Product Was Now Per kg Position
Luxury Wagyu Biltong — 1kg R650 R650 R650 Mid-premium. Above commodity biltong (R270–450/kg), below Woolworths free-range (R700/kg).
Luxury Wagyu Biltong — 500g R450 R325 R650 Now identical per-kilo to the 1kg. The smaller pack was penalising buyers — that is fixed.
Wagyu Biltong Gold — 1kg R1,450 R1,250 R1,250 Premium line. Above the highest openly quoted SA biltong price (R1,053/kg) by 19%.
Wagyu Biltong Gold — 7kg case R12,500 R8,400 R1,200 Now beats seven 1kg boxes (R8,750) by R350. The bulk case is finally the obvious choice.

Benchmarks: Butcher Brothers R269.99/kg · Vanni Vrystaat R279.90/kg · Biltong Boss R305.95/kg · Biltong Boytjies R349.99–449.99/kg · Mooiplaats Wagyu R600/kg · Woolworths free-range sliced R700/kg · Woolworths chilli snapsticks R1,053/kg (highest openly quoted SA price). Verified 28 Oct 2026.

Two doors, not one

Both China gates are open for Rwanda

1 May 2026 — China applied zero tariff to 100% of tariff lines on imports from the 53 African countries with diplomatic ties. Rwanda is an LDC origin, so that duty-free position has no expiry (other African origins hold it only to 30 April 2028).

20 July 2026 — coffee from all 53 African countries moved under a unified phytosanitary system. Reporting was explicit: for Rwanda, both doors open immediately.

Most of the market is still telling buyers one door opened. Both are open for us, and the phytosanitary unification is a compliance advantage worth having — it is not just a date.

Caviar — a 2027 proposition

We are not selling caviar until the paperwork exists.

Not yet available

The South African caviar permit stack is not assembled.

Caviar is not in the 2026 boxes, and we will not quote you a delivery date for it until a registered clearing agent has this stack in hand:

  1. DFFE — Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment
  2. ITAC frozen-fish notification
  3. DAFF importer registration
  4. SARS importer code and duty line
  5. NRCS conformity assessment
  6. CITES export permit and registered exporter code

A DAFF veterinary import permit is applied for at least four weeks before shipment and takes 5–10 working days to issue once approved — roughly two months end to end for a first shipment. Our December and January stock is reserved against existing customers.

Register interest and we will contact you the week the stack clears.
